baseline:
B
The attention mechanism allows the model to weigh the importance of different input elements, selectively focusing on the most relevant information for a given task, much like human attention.

B
Traditional encoder-decoder models compress the entire input sequence into a single fixed-size context vector, creating an information bottleneck. This makes it difficult to handle long sequences, as information from early tokens can be lost. Attention mechanisms solve this by allowing the decoder to look back at all the encoder's hidden states and focus on the most relevant parts of the input for each output token it generates.

C
Attention dynamically assigns importance scores (weights) to different parts of the input sequence. For each output token, it gives higher weights to the input tokens that are most relevant, allowing the model to "focus" on the right context.

B
The dot product is used to calculate the similarity between the Query vector and each Key vector. A higher dot product result indicates greater relevance, resulting in a higher attention score for the corresponding Value vector.

B
Self-attention allows the model to weigh the importance of all other tokens in the input sequence simultaneously when processing a single token. This parallel processing overcomes the sequential bottleneck of traditional models (like RNNs) and more effectively captures long-range dependencies.
